name: sol_am_fra_4
description: Commit-reveal scheme not bound to user address, enabling front-running/replay of commitments
question: The source file in `source` implements a commit-reveal scheme for sensitive on-chain actions (e.g., voting, registration, bidding) where the commit hash is computed only from action parameters (such as a secret or value) without including the committing user's address or a transaction-specific identifier, allowing an observer to front-run or replay/steal a revealed commitment by submitting it as their own, and this excludes schemes where the commitment already incorporates msg.sender or an unforgeable per-user nonce bound to the caller.
criteria: commit(bytes32 hash) stores hash = keccak256(secret, value) without mixing in msg.sender, so anyone observing the reveal can front-run using the same hash
reveal(secret, value) recomputes hash = keccak256(secret, value) and checks it against a stored commitment but never verifies the caller matches the original committer
A voting or auction commit function accepts a hash of the vote/bid content only, letting any address later claim that commitment as their own during reveal
The registration commit scheme hashes only the requested name and salt, omitting the registrant's address, enabling a third party to intercept and resubmit the same commitment
